mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative WORKPLACES mobility (-9.4% at t-0w, declining trend from -6.3%) indicates sustained workplace closure or remote work adoption. This suppresses commuting-linked retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -6.3% to -9.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds mean over last 28 days, or WORKPLACES recovers to above -5% while RETAIL_REC remains below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (2.3% → 5.6% → 4.1%) reflects increased essential-goods shopping frequency. Consumers making more frequent essential trips exhibit higher incidental retail-and-recreation visits during the same outings, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 4% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased from 2.3% to 5.6% between t-3w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above 4%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 2% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has risen from 0.3% to 4.1% over four weeks, signaling gradual public-transport recovery. Increased transit use enables broader mobility patterns and retail access, directly driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT exceeds 3% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from 0.3% at t-3w to 4.1% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining above 3%, or TRANSIT falls below 1% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between rising TRANSIT (4.1%) and elevated GROCERY_PHARM (4.1%) indicates consumers are both commuting and shopping. This dual mobility surge creates a multiplier effect: transit-enabled access combined with shopping frequency drives retail-and-recreation visits upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM exceed 3% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both series at or above 4% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 14 days when both TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM are above 3%, or either proxy falls below 2% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains deeply negative (-20.0% at t-0w, stable around -20% over four weeks), indicating outdoor recreation suppression. This constraint on outdoor leisure diverts discretionary time toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, producing a compensatory increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -18% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stable at -18% to -21% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining below -18%, or PARKS recovers above -10% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (4.7% to 5.6%, mean 5.2%) combined with suppressed WORKPLACES (-9.4%) indicates lockdown or work-from-home policy enforcement. Under this regime, retail-and-recreation venues remain restricted or operate at reduced capacity, constraining RETAIL_REC to remain negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 4.5% AND WORKPLACES falls below -8%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at 5.3% and WORKPLACES at -9.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15% over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 4.5% and WORKPLACES below -8%, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 4% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized around -24% over the past three weeks (t-3w: -24.4%, t-2w: -23.9%, t-1w: -23.0%, t-0w: -24.6%), indicating a persistent equilibrium. Absent a shock to TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, or GROCERY_PHARM, this trend-stationary pattern will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC near -24% over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged from -23.0% to -24.6% over four weeks with no directional trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds -20%, or any of TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, or GROCERY_PHARM shows a shock change of more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.

Consumers redirect leisure demand toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues accessible via transit, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -20.0% and TRANSIT at 4.1% at t-0w
